summary: Sequoia NF rock lookout built 1937-38 by the CCC and reached by stairs; destroyed by a structure fire on July 28, 2011; no source shows a replacement.

facts.design: L-4 cab with catwalk, 14 by 14 feet (NHLR); fire-lookouts.org calls it a C-3 style cab
facts.status_note: Destroyed by a structure fire on July 28, 2011; the sources read do not describe a replacement cabin
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Sequoia National Forest

events.note: CCC crew building a trail to the Needles; a stairway was needed up the rock
NHLR Built field gives 1938; Forest Service release says constructed 1937-38 by the CCC; fire-lookouts.org gives 1937
Millard R. James placed in charge when the new cabin opened in June 1939 (newspaper quoted on californialookouts.weebly.com)
270-acre fire started near the lookout in June 1972; Marie Cox ordered to evacuate, then went back on duty
Structure fire destroyed the lookout on July 28, 2011; cause under investigation per the Forest Service release
Forest Road 21S05, trail 32E22 and the rock formation closed during the fire

Hazardous materials removal completed October 2012; a Forest Service project lead proposed the rebuild, and the Kern and Tulare Counties Resource Advisory Committee awarded part of the requested funding

corrections.why: The NHLR page, the Forest Service release on it, and fire-lookouts.org give elevation, cab size and stairs, but none gives a tower height of 85.3 m (about 280 ft).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR and the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register give 8,020 ft (2,444 m). The Forest Service release and fire-lookouts.org give 8,245 ft, and two 1939 newspapers give 8,280 and 8,200 ft. The record keeps the NHLR value (2444.5 m).
NHLR gives 1938. The Forest Service release says 1937-38, fire-lookouts.org says 1937, and a June 1939 newspaper reports the cabin opening. The story reports the range.
NHLR calls it an L-4 cab with catwalk. Fire-lookouts.org calls it a C-3 style cab. Both are kept, and the story says the sources differ.

The Forest Service release says the cause was under investigation. A California lookouts page says reports indicated an ember from the wood stove. The story gives the official status first and the other account as reported.

notes_for_editor: Not verified: the record's 2007 rehab event (189 steps, Buck Rock Foundation) and the $13,000 rebuild figure. The buckrock.org and ponderosaca.com pages returned HTTP 404, and the December 2012 update gives no dollar amount. Recorder article (HTTP 429 on two tries) not read. California 2017 PDF yielded no Needles text. The record's kind two_story is not confirmed by these sources and is left unchanged. WebSearch budget was used up before this lookout, so no further searches were run.
